signal.title: otlptranslator: valid OTLP histogram stored with le="+Inf" below its own _count
signal.text: ### What did you do? On `main` at `44d6a0e0b`, translated a classic `HistogramDataPoint` whose explicit bounds end at `+Inf`, then read back its series: ```go pt.SetCount(42) pt.SetSum(100) pt.BucketCounts().FromRaw([]uint64{5, 10, 20, 7}) pt.ExplicitBounds().FromRaw([]float64{1, 2, math.Inf(1)}) ``` **Correction (2026-08-17):** this data point satisfies the arithmetic only on paper. `bucket_counts` is one longer than `explicit_bounds`, the bounds are strictly increasing, and `count` equals their sum (`5 + 10 + 20 + 7 = 42`) — but with `+Inf` as the last explicit bound the trailing bucket spans `(+Inf, +infinity)`, which cannot hold the 7 observations it is given, so `count = 42` is not attainable. The reachable shape is below. ### What did you expect to see? `le="+Inf"` equal to `_count`, as the cumulative convention requires. ### What did you see instead? Under which circumstances? `le="+Inf"` is written **twice** for the same series and timestamp, and nothing reports it. The two writes are equal whenever `count` equals the sum of the bucket counts **below** the infinite bound, which the reachable shape satisfies — so the defect there is the duplicate alone. They disagree, `_count` `42` against `le="+Inf"` `35`, when the counts below the bound do not add up to `count`, as in the example above, where the `7` sits in a bucket this path never reads. **The same input is rejected on the other path.** With `convert_histograms_to_nhcb: true` the identical data point becomes ``` {count:42, sum:100, [-Inf,1]:5, (1,2]:10, (2,+Inf]:20, (+Inf,+Inf]:7} ``` and `checkHistogramCustomBounds`, reached from `Histogram.Validate`, refuses it: ``` custom buckets: last +Inf bound must not be explicitly defined: histogram custom bounds must be finite ``` That rule is in `model/histogram/generic.go`, and `tsdb/head_append.go` turns it into a rejected sample by calling `h.Validate()`. It also looks deliberate rather than incidental: #17320 revisited that function to accept `-Inf` and kept `+Inf` rejected. So the invariant is already stated here, an explicit `+Inf` bound must not be defined, and the classic path is the one that does not hold to it — while being the default, since `convert_histograms_to_nhcb` is absent from `DefaultOTLPConfig`. **Where the second `le="+Inf"` comes from.** The loop over explicit bounds writes one `_bucket` series per bound, formatting the bound into `le`, so the `+Inf` bound emits `le="+Inf"` carrying the running sum at that point, `35`. Then `le="+Inf"` is synthesized again from `pt.Count()` after the loop. Both reach `Append` with identical labels and timestamp. Both are accepted and the commit keeps the first: two appends of `35` then `42` at the same timestamp in one batch return no error and store `35`, while the same second append issued after a commit is refused as a duplicate sample for that timestamp. The fourth bucket count, `7`, is the overflow bucket, which this path never reads. **Tests.** #19425 pins three shapes in `TestPrometheusConverter_AddHistogramDataPoints` — the reachable one and two that are invalid in different ways — and all three fail without the guard. **How often this happens — measured, and my first guess was wrong.** I wrote that an SDK has no reason to emit such a bound. The Go SDK accepts one: `AggregationExplicitBucketHistogram.err()` in `go.opentelemetry.io/otel/sdk/metric` validates only that the boundaries are monotonic, so `Boundaries{1, 2, math.Inf(1)}` is accepted with no error, and recording through it emits ``` explicit_bounds = [1 2 +Inf] bucket_counts = [5 2 3 0] (the trailing bucket is necessarily empty) count = 10 ``` so the input is reachable from a plain misconfiguration, though I still have not counted producers in the wild. It is worth fixing because nothing reports it: the bucket series stays monotonic, no error is returned, and the guard is one condition. #19425 carries the change, and reports the bound as a translation warning rather than repairing it silently, since the NHCB path refuses the same input. /cc @beorn7, who kept the explicit `+Inf` bound rejected in #17320, and @ArthurSens for `otlptranslator`. ### Prometheus version ```text prometheus, version (branch: main, revision: 44d6a0e0b1dbdcba4e68853d50e0bafc87d90507) build user: build date: go version: go1.26.1 platform: darwin/arm64 tags: unknown ```
signal.author: serhiy-bzhezytskyy

signal.title: promtool: no tool to find inconsistent classic histograms in a TSDB
signal.text: ### Proposal Quantiles, alerts and recording rules can be computed from classic histograms whose stored buckets contradict each other — and nothing lists which series are affected, or since when. **How the data gets there.** No ingest path cross-checks the float series of a classic histogram: scrape, remote write and the OTLP receiver append what was sent. Buckets whose cumulative counts decrease, or a `le="+Inf"` bucket disagreeing with `_count`, are stored as-is. Native histograms are rejected at append (`model/histogram/histogram.go:474`, `ErrHistogramCountMismatch`); classic ones have no equivalent check anywhere. **What it costs while it sits there.** `histogram_quantile` repairs non-monotonic input on the fly (`util/annotations/annotations.go:163`) and keeps returning plausible numbers, so SLOs and alerts built on an affected histogram are computed from silently patched data. The only signal is a per-query info annotation, phrased as a property of the query — the data stays broken for every next query. That annotation had to be taught to at least name the affected metric (#15411); finding all affected series in a TSDB still has no tool. **The fix.** `promtool tsdb check-histograms [db path]` scans a TSDB range (`--min-time`/`--max-time`) and reports, per histogram: non-monotonic cumulative buckets; `le="+Inf"` disagreeing with `_count`; `le` labels that do not parse as a float (`le="NaN"` is storable today); duplicate `le` spellings carrying different values at the same timestamp (`le="1"` vs `le="1.0"` on disjoint timestamps — the v3 migration shape — is recognized as clean); histograms with no `+Inf` bucket at all. Exits non-zero when anything is found, so it can run from cron or CI. Placed under `promtool tsdb` because it takes a database path like `dump` and `analyze` (`promtool check` takes config files and server URLs), and marked `[Experimental]` like `dump-openmetrics`. **Limits.** Native histograms are out of scope — already validated at append. And I have not measured how often such data occurs in the wild — this tool is how an operator answers that for their own TSDB. Found and verified on `main` at `44d6a0e`; file and line references are against that commit. cc @dgl — promtool is your path, and this proposes a new subcommand in it.

signal.title: storage/remote: pass RW 2.0 exemplars and metadata via AppendV2Options
signal.text: Part of #17632. **Stacked on top of #19251** — base branch is `krajo/rw2-receiver-appenderv2`, so review only the top commit here. ## What #19251 ported the RW 2.x receiver to `AppenderV2` but still appended exemplars and metadata through the standalone `AppendExemplar` / `UpdateMetadata` calls. This takes advantage of the combined `AppenderV2.Append`: for each received series, exemplars (sorted by timestamp, as the interface requires) and metadata are attached to the **first** sample/histogram append via `AppendV2Options`, and the remaining appends of the series carry empty options. ## Consequences - **Exemplar stats/errors** now come back as `storage.AppendPartialError` from that first `Append`. `X-Prometheus-Remote-Write-Written-Exemplars` is derived from it (`appended = provided − errored`); out-of-order exemplars still map to `400`, other exemplar errors remain a no-op — preserving prior behaviour. - **Metadata** is best-effort within `Append` and no longer reports an error, so the `samplesAppendedWithoutMetadata` increment is dropped from the RW 2.x path. The metric stays registered and is still used by the RW 1.0 path. No test asserts it. - `remoteWriteAppenderV2.UpdateMetadata` is removed (no longer used). ## Edge case Exemplars/metadata attach to the first sample/histogram, so if that first append is rejected (e.g. an out-of-order first sample) they are dropped with it; previously exemplars were appended in a separate pass. This only affects that specific case. ## Tests The mock's V2 appender now records `opts.Exemplars`/`opts.Metadata` and returns partial errors, so the existing V2-message assertions hold. Added a case exercising **metadata stored via AppendV2Options** — metadata storage was previously not covered by the handler test. ```release-notes NONE ```
signal.author: krajorama

signal.title: storage/remote: migrate Remote Write 2.x receiver to AppenderV2
signal.text: Part of #17632. **Stacked on top of #19250** (Remote Write 1.0 migration) — base branch is `krajo/rw1-receiver-appenderv2`, so review only the top commit here. Merge/rebase after #19250. ## What The Remote Write 2.x receiver path (`writeHandler.writeV2` / `appendV2`) is ported from V1 `storage.Appender` to `storage.AppenderV2`, matching the RW 1.0 path from #19250. - **Start timestamps** are now passed directly as the `AppenderV2.Append` `st` parameter; the appender owns ST zero-sample injection, so the explicit `AppendSTZeroSample` / `AppendHistogramSTZeroSample` calls (and the `handleHistogramZeroSample` helper) are removed. The receiver still gates on `ingestSTZeroSample`, which the same feature flag enables together with the TSDB/agent `EnableSTAsZeroSample` option (`cmd/prometheus/main.go`), so behaviour is preserved. - **Exemplars and metadata** keep using the standalone `AppendExemplar` / `UpdateMetadata` calls, now provided by `remoteWriteAppenderV2` via the optional `storage.ExemplarAppenderV2` / `storage.MetadataUpdaterV2` capabilities introduced in #19250. With both RW 1.0 and 2.x on `AppenderV2`, the V1 appendable is no longer used: `NewWriteHandler` drops its `storage.Appendable` parameter and the now-dead `remoteWriteAppender` wrapper is removed (net −52 lines). ## Tests The `write_handler` mock gained a V2 appender that injects ST zero samples, so the existing V2-message assertions (including the ST zero-sample expectations) continue to hold unchanged. ```release-notes NONE ```

signal.title: storage/remote: migrate Remote Write 1.0 receiver to AppenderV2
signal.text: Part of #17632. Alternative to #19248. Same goal (migrate the Remote Write 1.0 receiver to `AppenderV2`) but **without modifying the exported `storage.AppenderV2` interface**, so downstream `AppenderV2` implementations are not forced to change. ## What The RW 1.0 receiver path (`writeHandler.write`) is ported from V1 `storage.Appender` to `storage.AppenderV2`. RW 1.0 carries exemplars as a per-series list appended through a standalone `AppendExemplar` call, which `AppenderV2` (exemplars via `AppendV2Options`) does not offer. Instead of adding methods to `storage.AppenderV2`, this introduces two **optional capability interfaces**, `storage.ExemplarAppenderV2` and `storage.MetadataUpdaterV2`, discovered via a type assertion — the same idiom as `storage.GetRef`. The remote-write package composes them into the capability its receiver requires (`receiverAppenderV2`). Only Prometheus' own appenders on the RW path implement them: - **tsdb head**: `AppendExemplar`/`UpdateMetadata` moved to the shared `headAppenderBase` so both V1 and V2 appenders share one implementation; `initAppenderV2` delegates. - **tsdb agent**: the two methods moved to the shared `appenderBase`. - **fanoutAppenderV2**: delegates only to appenders that also implement the optional capability. - **remote-write `timestampTrackerV2`**: counts exemplars, metadata no-op. - **notReadyAppenderV2**: returns `ErrNotReady`. - **teststorage**: records via the optional capabilities. The Remote Write 2.x path (`writeV2`) still uses the V1 appendable and will be migrated separately. `NewWriteHandler` now takes both `appendable` and `appendableV2`; `web/api/v1` passes both. ## Why this shape `storage.AppenderV2` is implemented by downstream projects (e.g. Cortex/Mimir). Adding methods to it is a breaking change for them. Keeping exemplar/metadata as optional, assertion-discovered capabilities avoids that while still letting the receiver reuse the standalone-append shape. ## Tests - RW 1.0 handler tests now exercise the `AppenderV2` path (the mock appendable gained a V2 appender recording into the same slices, so existing assertions hold). - `TestHeadAppenderV2_AppendExemplarAndUpdateMetadata` verifies the head implements the optional capabilities and stores the exemplar (via `ExemplarQuerier`) and metadata. - teststorage's shared V2 appender test covers the optional methods (incl. `.Then` chaining). ```release-notes NONE ```

signal.title: Fix label mismatches in HA group alerts
signal.text: Two bugs prevented the following alerts from working correctly: 1. **PrometheusHAGroupNotIngestingSamples**: The `rate()` of `prometheus_tsdb_head_samples_appended_total` needs `sum without(type)` to strip the `type` label (added in Prometheus 3.x), otherwise the `and` with metadata/rules metrics fails to match and the alert never fires. The non-HA version of this alert already strips the type label correctly. 2. **PrometheusHAGroupCrashlooping**: The unclean restart branch tried to and an instance-level `prometheus_tsdb_clean_start` metric with a group-level restart ratio. These have different label sets so the and was always empty. Fixed by aggregating the clean_start check by HA group labels first. ```release-notes [BUGFIX] Mixins: Fix label mismatches that prevented PrometheusHAGroupNotIngestingSamples and PrometheusHAGroupCrashlooping from firing. ```

signal.title: promtool tsdb create-blocks-from rules panics on a rule file with multiple YAML documents
signal.text: ### What did you do? Ran `promtool tsdb create-blocks-from rules` over a rule file that contains a second YAML document. The file is otherwise valid, and the rule loader only means to warn that it will process the first document. `rules.yml`: ```yaml groups: - name: example rules: - record: job:http_requests:rate1m expr: sum by (job)(rate(http_requests_total[1m])) --- groups: [] ``` ```console $ promtool tsdb create-blocks-from rules \ --start=2026-08-01T00:00:00Z --end=2026-08-02T00:00:00Z \ --output-dir=./out rules.yml ``` No running Prometheus is needed to hit this. The rule files are loaded before the first range query is issued, so the process dies before it ever contacts `--url`. ### What did you expect to see? The warning that only the first document is processed, followed by the backfill running against the rules from that document. That is what `promtool check rules` does with the very same file: ```console $ promtool check rules rules.yml Checking rules.yml time=2026-08-16T17:03:40.271+08:00 level=WARN source=rulefmt.go:369 msg="Multiple document yaml rules files are not supported, only the first document is processed" SUCCESS: 1 rules found $ echo $? 0 ``` So the two commands disagree about the same file: one warns and succeeds, the other crashes. ### What did you see instead? Under which circumstances? A nil pointer dereference (frames in the middle elided): ```text time=2026-08-16T17:03:40.303+08:00 level=INFO source=rules.go:62 msg="new rule importer" component=backfiller start="01 Aug 26 00:00 UTC" end="02 Aug 26 00:00 UTC" panic: runtime error: invalid memory address or nil pointer dereference [signal SIGSEGV: segmentation violation code=0x1 addr=0x0 pc=0x905758] goroutine 1 [running]: log/slog.(*Logger).Handler(...) /usr/local/go/src/log/slog/logger.go:121 log/slog.(*Logger).log(0x0, ...) /usr/local/go/src/log/slog/logger.go:244 +0x98 log/slog.(*Logger).Warn(...) /usr/local/go/src/log/slog/logger.go:219 github.com/prometheus/prometheus/model/rulefmt.Parse(...) model/rulefmt/rulefmt.go:369 +0x373 github.com/prometheus/prometheus/model/rulefmt.ParseFile(...) model/rulefmt/rulefmt.go:396 +0x88 github.com/prometheus/prometheus/rules.FileLoader.Load(...) rules/manager.go:341 github.com/prometheus/prometheus/rules.(*Manager).LoadGroups(...) rules/manager.go:357 +0x12b main.(*ruleImporter).loadGroups(...) cmd/promtool/rules.go:75 ``` Note the receiver in the `log` frame is `0x0`: the logger the group loader holds is nil. It comes from `NewManager`. `ManagerOptions.Logger` is optional and gets a no-op logger when it is left unset: ```go if o.Logger == nil { o.Logger = promslog.NewNopLogger() } ``` but that runs *after* the default group loader has already been built out of the same field: ```go if o.GroupLoader == nil { o.GroupLoader = FileLoader{parser: o.Parser, logger: o.Logger} } ``` `FileLoader` captures the logger by value, so it keeps the nil forever, while `Manager.opts.Logger` ends up perfectly valid. That is why this went unnoticed: the manager looks like it has a logger, only its loader does not. Nothing dereferenced it until #18114 added the multi-document warning to `rulefmt.Parse`, which has no nil check: ```go err = decoder.Decode(&secondDoc) if !errors.Is(err, io.EOF) { logger.Warn("Multiple document yaml rules files are not supported, only the first document is processed") } ``` `promtool tsdb create-blocks-from rules` walks into it because its importer builds the manager without a logger, in `newRuleImporter`: ```go ruleManager: rules.NewManager(&rules.ManagerOptions{ NameValidationScheme: config.nameValidationScheme, }), ``` The backfill command is just the one caller that ships in this repo. Anything else that constructs a rule manager and leaves `ManagerOptions.Logger` unset is exposed in the same way, including projects that embed the rule manager as a library, so I would not treat this as promtool-specific. The Prometheus server itself is fine: `cmd/prometheus` always passes a logger. ### Affected versions Both halves arrived together in #18114 (merged 2026-04-09), which added the warning to `rulefmt.Parse` and the `logger` field to `FileLoader`. That commit is an ancestor of v3.12.0, so every release from v3.12.0 onwards is affected. I checked the current release, v3.13.2, and both sites still read the same there: - `rules/manager.go` builds `FileLoader` on line 171 and defaults the logger on line 187 - `cmd/promtool/rules.go` still calls `rules.NewManager` with only `NameValidationScheme` The maintenance lines do not carry it: neither v3.11.3 nor the v3.5.5 LTS has that commit as an ancestor, so they are not affected. ### Environment Reproduced against `main` at 7a73c9ae6 (`promtool` built from source, which is why the version output below is empty). * System information: ```text Linux 7.0.0-27-generic x86_64 ``` * Prometheus version: ```text promtool, version (branch: , revision: unknown) go version: go1.26.4 platform: linux/amd64 ``` * Prometheus configuration file: ```yaml # Not relevant, the crash happens in promtool while loading the rule file above. ``` ### Note on a fix Opened as #19433. It defaults the logger before the components that capture it are built, and adds a regression test that loads a multi-document rule file through a manager created from an empty `ManagerOptions`.
signal.author: thc1006

signal.title: rules: fix nil logger panic in the default group loader
signal.text: `ManagerOptions.Logger` is optional and `NewManager` substitutes a no-op logger when it is nil, but it only did so after building the default `FileLoader`, which captures the logger by value. A manager constructed without a logger therefore ends up with a perfectly valid `opts.Logger` and a nil one inside its group loader, which is why this stayed hidden for a while. Nothing dereferenced it until #18114 added the multi-document warning to `rulefmt.Parse`, so today loading a rule file with a second YAML document panics. `promtool tsdb create-blocks-from rules` walks into it because its importer builds the manager without a logger, and so does any other caller that leaves the field unset. Details and a reproduction are in #19432. The change moves the defaulting up, ahead of everything that captures the logger: ```go if o.Context == nil { o.Context = context.Background() } // Default the logger first: the components built below capture it by value, // so substituting it afterwards would leave them holding a nil logger. if o.Logger == nil { o.Logger = promslog.NewNopLogger() } ``` Nothing between the old and the new position reads `o.Logger`, so this is a reordering rather than a behaviour change: `FileLoader` is the only construction site that touches it. ## About the test The regression test goes through exported API only, since that is the shortest path to the nil: a manager built from an empty `ManagerOptions` loading a fixture with a second YAML document. ```go ruleManager := NewManager(&ManagerOptions{}) var ( groups map[string]*Group errs []error ) require.NotPanics(t, func() { groups, errs = ruleManager.LoadGroups(time.Second, labels.EmptyLabels(), "", nil, false, "fixtures/rules_multi_doc.yaml") }) ``` On `main` it fails with the panic: ```text --- FAIL: TestManager_LoadGroups_WithoutLogger (0.00s) Error: func (assert.PanicTestFunc)(0x1145080) should not panic Panic value: runtime error: invalid memory address or nil pointer dereference log/slog.(*Logger).log(0x0, ...) github.com/prometheus/prometheus/model/rulefmt.Parse(...) github.com/prometheus/prometheus/rules.FileLoader.Load(...) ``` and passes with the change. `go test ./rules/...` is otherwise unaffected, and I also ran `./cmd/...` and `./web/...` since they build managers of their own. ## Why not guard the call in rulefmt `rulefmt.Parse` could nil-check before `logger.Warn` instead, but then every future consumer of a `FileLoader` logger needs the same guard, and `NewManager` already promises a non-nil logger to everything it constructs. Repairing that promise seemed better than defending against it at each call site. I am happy to swap it round if you would rather have the check in `rulefmt`, or to add both. #### Which issue(s) does the PR fix: Fixes #19432 #### Release notes for end users (**ALL** commits must be considered). ```release-notes [BUGFIX] Rules: Fix a panic when a rule manager created without a logger loads a rule file containing multiple YAML documents. ```

signal.title: promql: fix panic in extendFloats on a series with an empty window
signal.text: `extendFloats` dereferences `floats[len(floats)-1]` with no emptiness check, and `matrixSelector` calls it for every series the querier returned. A series can be returned and then trimmed to nothing — selection is per chunk, trimming is per sample — so a chunk that *spans* the query window without holding a sample inside it yields an empty slice: ``` demo_metric[10s] -> 200, matrix, 0 series demo_metric[10s] anchored -> 422 unexpected error: runtime error: index out of range [-1] demo_metric[10s] smoothed -> 422 unexpected error: runtime error: index out of range [0] with length 0 ``` Two messages from one hole: `anchored` leaves the index at `len-1` == -1 (Go omits the length suffix for a negative index), `smoothed` recomputes it as `sort.Search(-1, …)` == 0. Any scrape gap longer than `range + lookbackDelta` reaches this when queried inside the gap, since the modifiers widen the sample window by `lookbackDelta`; reproduced against the released `prom/prometheus:v3.13.2` image by killing a real target for 40s. The panic is recovered, so this is a 422 and a logged stack trace per attempt, not a crash. **The fix** returns the empty slice before indexing, as-is rather than a fresh `[]FPoint{}` so the caller can still pool it. That matches #17479, which fixed `resets`/`changes` to return empty for anchored selectors when the samples are outside the range. `extendFloats` has exactly two callers, both in `matrixSelector`, so this is the whole reachable surface — `rate(foo[2m] anchored)` goes through `extendedRate` and was already correct. Whether such a series should reach `matrixSelector` at all is a larger question this PR does not touch. **Tests:** five `promqltest` cases in `extended_vectors.test` — the two panicking queries, the no-modifier control, and two asserting extension still produces the right values when the window does contain samples. The two panic cases were confirmed to fail on an unpatched tree. #### Which issue(s) does the PR fix: <!-- No issue filed; reported directly as this PR. --> #### Release notes for end users (**ALL** commits must be considered). ```release-notes [BUGFIX] PromQL: Fix a panic in range selectors using the experimental `anchored` or `smoothed` modifier when the selected series has no samples inside the query window, for example a query evaluated inside a scrape gap. ```
signal.author: CharlieTLe

signal.title: scrape: go test -shuffle aborts the test run with "select on synctest channel from outside bubble"
signal.text: Root cause is upstream in Go's `net`, which I reported as golang/go#80903. It needs a change here regardless: the upstream fix covers two of the three channels involved, and the third is the one this hits on the default resolver path. ### What did you do? Ran the `scrape` package's own tests with Go's test shuffling enabled, on a clean checkout of `main` at `7a73c9ae6`: ``` go test -count=1 -shuffle=42 ./scrape/ ``` ### What did you expect to see? The same result as the default order, which passes. ### What did you see instead? Under which circumstances? The run aborts. No test is reported as failing — the process is gone first: ``` fatal error: select on synctest channel from outside bubble goroutine 2196 [running]: net.cgoLookupIP ← net.(*Resolver).lookupIP ← internal/singleflight.(*Group).doCall created by internal/singleflight.(*Group).DoChan in goroutine 1823 FAIL github.com/prometheus/prometheus/scrape 1.745s ``` `-shuffle` appears in no workflow, so the default order is the only one CI runs, which is why this passes upstream on every commit. Nine tests in this package reach `osutil.GetFQDN`, and the fatal needs the `synctest` one — `TestScrapeOffsetDistribution`, through `setOffsetSeed` — to be the **first** lookup in the process; once an outside caller has reached the resolver, the in-bubble one is harmless. Measured two ways: each of the other eight can abort when paired with it, and on one such pair ten seeds split cleanly by which test ran first. It is not the `singleflight` group the stack trace suggests: the object is a package-level channel in `net`, created lazily under a `sync.Once`, so whoever calls first decides which bubble it belongs to for the rest of the process. The full write-up is in golang/go#80903. `manager.go:390-393` already describes the hazard, and `setupSynctestManager` avoids it with a fake server, a `net.Pipe` per dial and `skipJitterOffsetting`. `TestScrapeOffsetDistribution` is the one `synctest` site that doesn't go through the helper, and the lookup isn't in the scraping path a fake network covers: it arrives from `ApplyConfig` → `setOffsetSeed`. Setting the existing flag on that test isn't a way out on its own: ``` --- FAIL: TestScrapeOffsetDistribution scrape_test.go:8033: "1" is not greater than "2" Expected targets to be scraped at staggered offsets rather than simultaneously at scrape index 0 ``` The flag does two things at once: it skips the seed calculation, and at `scrape.go:1313` it zeroes each scrape loop's offset — which is what that test asserts. The three tests using the helper depend on the second effect; this one needs the first and cannot have the second. Fixing it here does not depend on the upstream fix landing: the third channel, `net.threadLimit`, derives its capacity from `rlim.Cur`, so it cannot simply be created eagerly, and with the other two changed the default resolver path on this platform still aborts. Related: `#17941`, though the mechanism there is different. ### System information ``` darwin/arm64, go1.26.1 ``` ### Prometheus version ``` Reproduced from source at 7a73c9ae6, not from a release binary. ``` ### Prometheus configuration file ``` n/a — this is a test-suite failure, no configuration involved. ```
signal.author: serhiy-bzhezytskyy

signal.title: scrape: keep the FQDN lookup out of synctest bubbles
signal.text: `go test -shuffle` can kill the `scrape` test run: the process aborts, no test is reported as failing, and CI never sees it because `-shuffle` is in no workflow. One in-bubble name lookup is enough to arm it — `TestScrapeOffsetDistribution` resolves the host's FQDN from inside a `synctest` bubble, and any later lookup from outside aborts the process. The root cause is in Go's `net`, which I reported as golang/go#80903 and sent a fix for as golang/go#80906 — and that upstream fix does not remove the need for this change. `skipJitterOffsetting` would keep the lookup out, but it also zeroes each scrape loop's offset — exactly what this test asserts, which is why it cannot use the synctest helper. So the FQDN gets its own private option, in the same shape: the helper and that one test supply a fixed value, the offset seed stays real, and no lookup happens inside a bubble. Verified against the twelve configurations that were fatal on `main` rather than a fresh set — four shuffle seeds of the whole package, and eight pairings of this test with another that resolves, each at its own fatal seed — and all twelve pass here. Instrumented, no `GetFQDN` call has `synctest` on the stack, against one on `main`. The new test fails if the helper stops setting the option; I checked by removing the line. What it does not cover: the option is set directly in `TestScrapeOffsetDistribution`, so nothing catches its removal there, and the crash that would return is one CI cannot see. Upstream covers two of the three channels `net` creates lazily; the third, `net.threadLimit`, takes its capacity from `rlim.Cur`, so it cannot be created eagerly — and with the other two fixed, the default resolver path here still aborts. cc @krajorama #### Which issue(s) does the PR fix: Fixes #19439 #### Release notes for end users (**ALL** commits must be considered). ```release-notes NONE ```
signal.author: serhiy-bzhezytskyy

signal.title: discovery/ionos: don't panic on absent response containers
signal.text: [PR 19418](https://redirect.github.com/prometheus/prometheus/pull/19418) guarded the leaf fields of the IONOS server discovery, but the pointers holding those leaves were left unchecked. `Items`, `properties` and `ips` are all pointers carrying `omitempty` in `ionos-cloud/sdk-go/v6`, so a response can legitimately omit any of them: ```go for _, server := range *servers.Items { // omitted when the datacenter has no servers ... if server.Properties.AvailabilityZone != nil // Properties itself may be absent ``` Nothing under `discovery/` recovers, so each of these takes down the whole Prometheus process rather than degrading the target. Guarded here, each covered by a subtest that panics without the fix: - `servers.Items` — a datacenter holding no servers. This is the cheapest one to hit: an empty datacenter returns a collection with no `items` member at all. - `server.Entities.Nics.Items` — a server whose NIC collection carries no items. - `nic.Properties` and `nic.Properties.Ips` — a NIC with no properties, or with properties but no addresses. - `server.Properties` — now read through a local that falls back to the zero value, which keeps the existing per-field checks as the single place where a label is omitted, rather than wrapping two separate blocks in a nil check. - `BootCdrom.Id` and `BootVolume.Id` — the reference is present but carries no id. `ResourceReference.Id` is a pointer. - `server.Entities.Volumes.Items` and `volumes[0].Properties`. An absent `ips` is treated as an empty one, so a NIC without addresses behaves exactly as it already did for `"ips": []`. The cases run through the real SDK decoder rather than constructing structs, so the nil pointers are the ones a live API would produce. They are separate responses instead of extra entries in `testdata/servers.json` because the first panic would otherwise mask the other seven. I have no IONOS account to confirm this end to end, so the change rests on the field types and their `omitempty` tags in `ionos-cloud/sdk-go/v6 v6.3.11`. ```release-notes [BUGFIX] IONOS SD: Do not panic when the API response omits the server, NIC or volume collections, or a server's properties. ```
signal.author: ekalinin

signal.title: feat(promql): add ignore_start_times() function to disable start timestamp processing per-query
signal.text: This adds a new experimental PromQL function ignore_start_times() that allows users to selectively disable start time processing on a per-query basis. This addresses issue #19264 where users need a way to ignore bad start times from exporters without disabling start time processing globally. The function works by temporarily disabling useStartTimestamps when evaluating its argument, then returning the result with start timestamps ignored. Fixes #19264 ```release-notes [FEATURE] PromQL: Add ignore_start_times() function to disable start timestamp processing per-query. ```
